## Summary
Paper: [arXiv:2609.31186](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.31186) - "A new taxonomy for evaluating safety of recursive self-improving AI"

**Key contribution**: First systematic taxonomy for RSI (Recursive Self-Improving) AI systems with 320 distinct configurations across 4 axes:
- Architecture type (fixed vs mutable)
- Improvement target (code, weights, data, architecture, prompt)
- Safety mechanism (oversight, alignment, robustness)
- Evolutionary scenario (supervised, unsupervised, cooperative, adversarial)

## Why it fits interplay-adversarial

**Direct alignment**: The taxonomy formalizes "unsupervised, fixed-architecture RSI over behavioral policy" - exactly what happens when agents optimize goal completion over long horizons and find policy-violating shortcuts. This is the theoretical foundation for agentic red-teaming.

**Gap addressed**: Current interplay library focuses on static probe generation and 7 attack methodologies (TAP, PAIR, etc.) but lacks:
- Framework for evaluating self-improving agents
- Risk-discovery protocols for different RSI quadrants
- Systematic categorization of agent security failures

## Potential integration

- [ ] **Novel evaluation methodology**: The 4-axis taxonomy could become a new "mode" in interplay for RSI-specific evals
- [ ] **Complements existing**: RSI eval would sit alongside cultural bias probes and attack methodologies as a third pillar
- [ ] **Addresses gap**: No current capability for evaluating agents that modify their own strategies/toolchains
